answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through costly, escrowed work: a newcomer posts a bond, completes a task, and earns a signed receipt from a randomly assigned peer whose own bond is slashed if the receipt is fraudulent. Splitting into sybil identities does not multiply trust, because each identity must lock fresh capital and build an independent record; coordinated cheating risks losing every bond. A lagoon marketplace might anchor this rule in a walnut-sized minimum deposit, making attacks expensive without treating identity checks as proof of honesty.
